001: Ivan, I heard you found a part-time job at a cafe. How do you like it?
Yes, Anna, I've been working there for two weeks now. I really like it.
And what do you do there?
Mostly I take orders and serve coffee. Sometimes I help in the kitchen.
Sounds good. And is the schedule convenient?
It's fine. I work in the evenings, after classes.
002: Dmitry, do you know where a student can find a part-time job?
I do, the library is actually looking for an assistant. I saw a notice there yesterday.
Really? And what do you have to do?
Put books back on the shelves and help readers find the materials they need.
That's probably a calm job. And how much do they pay?
Not very much, but the schedule is flexible and you can study for your classes.
003: Sergey, are you still working as a courier?
Yes, but I want to quit. It's really hard to get around the city in winter.
I understand, it must be cold and you get very tired.
Exactly. Plus the pay is unstable, it all depends on the number of orders.
Haven't you thought about finding something in an office?
I have, but so far I can't make it work with my studies.
004: Olga, I saw you work at a clothing store. How's it going?
Everything's great, Maria! They even praised me for my good work with customers.
That's great! And what are your duties?
I advise customers, help them pick the right size, and process their purchases.
It's probably interesting, but it must be tiring to stand all day.
Yeah, by the evening my legs ache, but I really enjoy talking to people.
005: Alexey, you said you wanted to find a part-time job as a tutor. Did it work out?
Yes, Elena, I found a schoolboy. I do math with him twice a week.
Great! And how did you find him?
Through acquaintances, the boy's mom asked me to help.
And how do you like teaching?
Turns out it's pretty hard, but interesting. I prepare for every lesson.
006: Maria, I heard you got a half-time job at an office. How do you like it?
Everything's good, Anna. The work isn't hard, but it requires attention to detail.
And what exactly do you do?
I answer calls, type up documents, and help with reports.
Sounds serious. And are your colleagues nice?
Yes, very friendly. Everyone helps if I don't understand something.
007: Ivan, are you still working on the weekends?
Yes, Dmitry, I have a part-time job at a sports club. I help at the front desk.
Don't you want to rest on Saturday and Sunday?
Of course I do, but I need the money. Plus, I can work out there for free.
That's a big plus! And is the shift long?
Six hours, but the time flies by.
008: Elena, you said you were looking for a part-time job with a flexible schedule. Did you find one?
Yes, Olga, now I work as a babysitter for a family in the evenings.
Is that convenient? I mean, in the evening you probably want to rest.
Sometimes I get tired, but the kids are calm and the pay is good.
And what do you do with them?
I help with homework, read them books, and play board games.
009: Sergey, I found out there's a lab assistant position at the university. Have you tried it?
No, Alexey, what do you have to do there?
Help professors prepare materials for classes and check the equipment.
Sounds interesting. And is it a paid job?
Yes, a small salary, but it's good for your future career.
Then I'll definitely submit an application. Thanks for telling me!
010: Anna, do you regret getting a job at the restaurant?
No, Maria, not one bit. I've learned a lot during this time.
I've gotten better at understanding people and learned how to work in a team.
That's very valuable. And in the future, do you want to stay in this field?
I don't know, but for now I like it, and I enjoy my work.
